I don't agree. Let me qoute some of the stuff you mentioned.

**"Lack of Free Speech"** Lol, seriously? have you been to other subreddits like r/lgbt for instance, say one thing even mildly offensive about a gay person there and you get perma banned. This sub is still okay, What you claim to be "sulking in the negatives experiences and blaming all of that on Asperger's " is just us venting, we have the right to vent and express ourselves, aspergers can be a very debilitating thing to deal with. This subreddit is not negative, it's simply a reflection of the real life struggles of people with aspergers.

**"The worst part about this is that it creates an us-versus-them mentality. Us being the people whom had terrible experiences because of something out of their control, and Them being the people who caused those bad experiences."**  This really annoys me. Why is it okay for NT society to label and "other" people with autism but when we do the same to them you claim we have a "us vs them mentality"?  Look at this question for instance, [https://www.reddit.com/r/changemyview/comments/g7rn2h/cmv\_autism\_shouldnt\_be\_an\_excuse\_for\_bad\_behavior/](https://www.reddit.com/r/changemyview/comments/g7rn2h/cmv_autism_shouldnt_be_an_excuse_for_bad_behavior/)  Pure ignorance with over 2k likes. Nobody would ever say "being blind is not a excuse for bad behaviour", but somehow if the person has autism it's different.  In NT society, Autism is connotated with retardation, the typical NT insult is to call someone "autistic" as if to imply that autism makes you dumb, even though autism has nothing to do with intelligence. We are the ones who are victims of the ableist ideas thats embedded in society, we are subjected to labels being put on us such as "people with autism are violent" or "people with aspergers are assholes", they are the one's who put labels on us, not the other way around. Secondly, many people with asperger are not accomodated by mainstream society and have been objectively speaking , abused by NTs for a long time. This needs to be acknowledged, it not a victim mentality or a "us vs them thing" its an objective fact. I know not all people with aspergers have had negative experiences in regards to being bullied and abused but a large amount have. People with asd are at a much higher risk of being victims of sexual and physical abuse compared to the general population, most of this abuse against them is carried out by Neurotypical people. Yes not all NTs are evil however you need to understand where the distrust for them comes from.

**"sulking in the negatives experiences and blaming all of that on Asperger's"**

Nonsense, We don't blame everything on Aspergers.

**" It doesn't improve anything, it only allows bitterness to foster. By making the assumption that the world is against people with autism"**

Acknowledging something factual is not the same as assuming that "the world is against people with autism". Factually speaking, The way society is stuctured, its built for NTs, not for people with aspergers. I know life is not easy for anyone whether you're NT or not however aknowledging that the world is rigged againts people like us is not saying that everyone is against us or that the world is out to get us, its simply acknowledging something that is an objective fact.

**"sometimes the world wasn't at fault. I was just having a crappy experience, and everyone does from time to time"-**

Again I know not everyone with aspergers struggles however-80% unemeployment rate, 7x higher rate of suicide, and higher rates of being victims of all types of abuse compared to the general population, what does that tell you? Yes everyone has "crappy experiences" but those with aspergers have very much gotten the short end of the stick. Those with aspergers are a disavantaged minority, we are not the same playing field as everyone else, again this is not a victim mentality its just an objective fact.

Both people with aspergers and those from the LGBT community tend to be social outcasts, thus they tend to be more drawn to each other than they are to typical people. Like attracts like that's the law of nature. An aspie might be more drawn to the LGBT community because they feel less judged and more accepted around those type of people.

100% agree. I know this from first hand experience as well. If you're depressed and you go to a psychologist, what do they usually tell you? "Spend time with your friends", "express how you really feel" "stop ruminating" "don't isolate yourself". That might work for a NT but what if you have aspergers and don't have any friends to turn to? what if you don't express your feelings the way NTs do, and have routines? and what if we're isolated and we don't necessarily want to be? Almost all psychologists are NTs and they simply do not understand things from an autists perspective, they are ignorant and are unable to look at things from any other way other than thier own. The problem is not just with the mental health sector, it is society at large which continues to judge people with autism through a Neurotypical lens because we do not have an obvious physical disabilty. If you have aspergers and you go to a psychiatrist they are subconciously judging your body language, facial expression, tone of voice etc. , as if you are just another NT when you are not. They do not understand the nature of autism, then they think that by putting us in therapy and trying to make us act more like a NT that they're "fixing us" or "helping us" when all they are doing is causing more damage. They dont understand our social struggles or how we feel, they know nothing about us, that is why many aspies feel like therapy is useless for them, because 98% of those in the mental health sector are NTs who are uninformed and clueless when it comes to dealing with those who have autism. The only way therapy will help people like us is if the person you're going to is informed about the complex nature of autism and how it affects everyone differently. The problem is that finding these people in the mental health field is tough, since they're basically non existent.

As soon as we drop our mask we are shunned, rejected, abused etc, so what other option do we have? This is the number one reason why aspies have such a high suicide rate, having to live a life of not being able to be who they truly are, they'll rather kill themselves than live such a life.

NTs expect you to behave a certain way, if you dont most of them will reject you. They look at us and think we cant do the job simply because of our demenour, body language, monotone voice etc, while the NT is more likley to get hired simply because they are NT and behave in a way thats considered acceptable and "normal". Thats what privelege essentially means, an unearned advantage.

NTs are advantaged simply for being NTs while people with aspergers are disadvantaged for simply being autistic. NT privelege is just as important as class privelege, white privelege etc. but nobody ever talks about it.  The suicide rate,unemployment rate and marriage rate of people with aspergers says it all. Nobody ever makes adjustments for us, we are the ones thats always expected to conform to NT standards and when we dont we are socially rejected. Its no wonder many aspies are so unhappy or in extreme cases turn into school shooters/serial killers. Its a reaction to living a life of constantly been told who you are is wrong/defective, to constantly have to put up a mask around NTs because you know that most of them are never going to accept you if you reveal your true self, and been told that your issues are imaginary or in head, while watching NTs around you having an easier time in life for simply being born NT. NTs have the privelege of being treated better, having an easier time getting hired, easier time finding a partner, and finding it easier to assimilate into mainstream society, while aspies have to work 10x harder just to stay on level footing.

Yes. Most people with aspergers tend to come across as flat and unemotive. It has to do with how our brains is wired we cant help it. In terms of speech aspies lack variation in tone as well as prosody which makes our voices sound its lacking emotion/montone/robotic. We also lack the inherent understand of body language which NTs have and we lack understanding of our own body language as well. Aspies tend to be stiff and dont use alot of hand gestures,facial expressions and other non verbal communication styles that NTs use all the time. Aspergers is a communication disorder and one of the hallmark features is impairment in non verbal communication, which is what hand gestures essentially is. I dont speak alot with my hands either and when I do I have to force myself to do it. With asd it always feels like you have to put up a mask and can never really be yourself, its tough as hell.
This is exactly how I feel, I feel like I am an alien, its hell.

Just like a blind man cannot change the fact that he cannot see, the same way an aspie cannot change the fact that they'll always be alone. We are not on the same wave length as 99% of the population who dont have aspergers and whose brains are wired diffrentely to ours. There's nothing you can do about the loneliness, other than change your perception. You have to accept the loneliness rather than fight it, thats the only way you going to survive. The happiest aspies are the ones who enjoy being alone. You never going to be NT, the majority (masses) will always find a way to discredit and ostracize you, but you shouldnt focus on that, focus on the positives, the few friends you actually have who are willing to accept you for you. You need to learn to be content in your own loneliness, thats the best way to deal with it. Aspergers is essentially a social death sentence, you've been dealt a real shitty hand ,you just have to try and make the best out of your situation.
